title: Maths reference: Year 8 Measurement
summary: The words and methods from Year 8 Measurement, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/measurement-8 (see snippets/maths-algebra-7.json for the format; split from the strand courses' card files on 1 Nov 2026).

items.label: rate
items.hint: A rate compares quantities with different units (km per h, $ per kg); a ratio compares the same kind. 1 km/h = 1000 m ÷ 3600 s: divide by 3.6 for m/s.
items.board:
widget: rate
top: km, distance
bottom: h, time
rate: 60
x: 2.5
items.shows: At 60 km per hour, 2.5 hours matches 150 km

items.label: using a rate
items.hint: Write the units in: km ÷ km/h = h. Then check the size makes sense.

items.label: model assumptions
items.hint: Every model assumes something (steady speed, no fees, no starting charge). When it disagrees with real life, name the assumption and refine the model.

items.label: composite area
items.hint: Cut the shape into pieces you know and add their areas, or take the missing pieces away from a big rectangle. Each piece uses its own lengths.
items.board:
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 8,0; 8,3; 3,3; 3,6; 0,6
split: on
units: m
items.shows: An L-shape with its side lengths

items.label: estimating an irregular area
items.hint: Count the full squares, add half the part squares, multiply by the area of one square. A finer grid gives a closer estimate.

items.label: volume and capacity
items.hint: A cubic metre is 100 × 100 × 100 = 1 000 000 cm³: convert each of the three lengths.

items.label: area of a circle
items.hint: Slices of a circle make a near-rectangle πr long and r high. The area is between 2r² and 4r². Do not mix it up with C = 2πr.
items.board:
widget: circlearea
r: 3
n: 24
cut: shown
units: cm
items.shows: 24 slices laid top to tail: nearly a rectangle πr by r

items.label: radius from area
items.hint: Divide by π, then take the square root. A semicircle is half the area; its perimeter is half the circumference plus the diameter.

items.label: Pythagoras' theorem
items.hint: In a right-angled triangle, the squares on the two shorter sides add to the square on the hypotenuse c, the side opposite the right angle.
items.board:
widget: pythag
a: 3
b: 4
units: cm
items.shows: Squares of 9, 16 and 25 on a 3-4-5 triangle

items.label: finding a side
items.hint: Add the squares for the hypotenuse; subtract for a shorter side. Check: the hypotenuse is the longest.

items.label: right, acute or obtuse
items.hint: With c the longest side: equal, right-angled; a² + b² smaller, obtuse; bigger, acute. Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and multiples.

items.label: time zones
items.hint: Find the difference between the UTC offsets, add or take it away, and change the day if you cross midnight. For a flight, add the flight time in the departure zone, then change zones.
